names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 17 mai, «Sfântul Nou Mucenic Nicolae din Metsovo».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 17 Μαΐου, «Άγιος Νικόλαος εκ Μετσόβου», with the rank word and the town left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог's heading for 16. мај ст. ст., „Свети новомученик Николај.“ Свети is not a rank; новомученик is the `new-martyr` this folder carries in `types`; strip them and the heading leaves a bare forename and nothing else — the Epirus, the Trikala and the 1617 are all in the body and none of them is part of the name. **A deliberate exact-form fold, measured with `foldchk.py` before drafting**: `nicholas-of-pskov` already carries „Николај“ as its `sr` form, off this same book's Julian 28 February, where he is „Свети блажени Николај, јуродиви псковски“ — a fool for Christ of Pskov dead in 1576, against a new martyr of Epirus beheaded at Trikala in 1617. Two days, two accounts, two men; the fold is read in this batch's commit message. The spelling is this book's own, Николај and not Никола, and is stored as printed.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 17 mai — «Sfântul Nou Mucenic Nicolae din Metsovo»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 17ης Μαΐου — «Άγιος Νικόλαος εκ Μετσόβου»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 17 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same civil day the Romanian calendar already keeps him on, and it is plainly the same man, the neomartyr of Metsovo in Epirus. **The page's own notes give a second day and it is not taken**: «Ορισμένοι συναξαριστές, όπως του Αγίου Νικοδήμου του Αγιορείτου, αναφέρουν τη μνήμη του Aγίου Νικολάου εκ Μετσόβου στις 16 Μαΐου» — some synaxaria, Nikodemos the Hagiorite's among them, put his memory on 16 May — and the same note says he was formally entered in the Orthodox calendar in 1988 by the Ecumenical Patriarchate, at the request of the metropolitan of Trikke and Stagoi, and «Τιμάται στις 17 Μαΐου». One row per church is the schema, the day page and the page head agree on the seventeenth, and the sixteenth is recorded here. **He is not the day's other Nicholas**: saint.gr keeps a Nicholas the great martyr of Bulgaria, dead in 1555, on this same day, who is a new folder in batch `el-05-17`. **The Greek adds his surname and his two bynames**, Basdanis, Vlachonikolas and Exintatrichis, and his death year 1617 in the head line; the existing folder carries no `dates` object and is not given one here. **It adds the whole of the fall and the recovery**: the bakery at Trikala, the forced conversion, the return to Metsovo, the Turkish barber who caught him selling kindling and made him promise a load a year, and the decision never to compromise again. **It names the two services written for him**, by Nikolaos Kyrkos or Tzartzoulis of Metsovo, printed at Venice in 1757 and 1771, and by the hymnographer Gerasimos of Mikragiannanita in the Epirot Leimonarion of 1968 — but it prints neither, so no hymn is taken. **Dionysios the Philosopher, metropolitan of Trikke, is named** and sent to 10 October; the corpus does not keep him, so he is named without a link.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 29.05.2026 (16. мај ст. ст.) — „Свети новомученик Николај.“

attestations.note: **`sr-cand.mjs`'s day list could not see this folder, and the reason is on the folder already.** The Romanian and Greek rows keep him on the menologion **17/5** and the Prologue keeps him on the **16/5**, so the day list, which matches on the menologion number, offered eighteen folders and not this one. **What settles it is a sentence this corpus already holds**: this folder's own life records that saint.gr's page says „some synaxaria, Nikodemos the Hagiorite's among them, keep his memory on 16 May“, and that the seventeenth is the day of his formal entry in the calendar by the Ecumenical Patriarchate in 1988. **The Prologue is one of those synaxaria.** The identification is then exact on every particular the entry gives: „Родом из Епира“ against a folder named for Metsovo in Epirus; „мучен од Турака“ against a `new-martyr` under Ottoman rule; „посечен у Трикали“ against a life whose whole scene is Trikala in Thessaly; and „1617. године“ against saint.gr's head line of 1617. **Two days and four churches, and it is not a conflict**: the Romanian and Greek rows stay on 17 May and neither was moved. **A FIRST DATE FOR A FOLDER THAT HELD NO `dates` OBJECT**: `death` 1617, the year both books give, so nothing to widen. **New here, and the Prologue is the only book that tells the end**: that he was **beheaded**, where saint.gr's life breaks off at his resolve and names no manner of death at all; that **his head is kept to this day in one of the monasteries of Meteora in Thessaly**; and that he **works many wonders, heals the gravest sicknesses and is known above all for driving the locusts off the fields**. `types` untouched — новомученик is the `new-martyr` the folder carries, and „Чини многа чудеса“ is wonders worked and not the Чудотворац title. No `locations`, although Epirus, Trikala, Meteora and Thessaly are all named, as the Greek page already names Metsovo and Trikala; this folder has never carried coordinates. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

death.note: The Охридски пролог for 16. мај ст. ст.: „За веру Христову мучен од Турака и посечен у Трикали 1617. године.“ The same year stands in saint.gr's head line for him, which this folder's life records as „dead, by saint.gr's head line, in 1617“; the folder held no `dates` object at all until now, and doxologia names no year.
